title: Anthropic Launches Claude Opus 5, Closing the Gap With Fable 5 at Half the Price
excerpt: The new model targets everyday coding and office tasks with near-flagship performance, as the AI startup prepares for an IPO and cements a $5 billion AMD partnership.
body:
• Anthropic launched Claude Opus 5 on Friday, a model it says nears Fable 5's capabilities at roughly half the cost.
  • Opus 5 is optimized for daily coding and office work, with improved safety over its predecessor Opus 4.8.
  • GitHub Copilot added Opus 5 support on launch day, expanding the model's reach across developer tools.
  • The release comes days after AMD committed a $5 billion equity investment in Anthropic and two gigawatts of GPU capacity.

Anthropic on Friday launched Claude Opus 5, its latest AI model that the San Francisco-based startup says approaches the capabilities of its more powerful Fable 5 at half the price. The release marks the first major Opus upgrade since version 4.8 in May and lands as the company accelerates toward what reports describe as an IPO later this year.

In an interview with Reuters, Anthropic product leader Dianne Penn said the model was designed for the tasks that occupy most of a developer's or office worker's day: writing and reviewing code, answering complex questions, and handling routine knowledge work.

"We're building and continue to consistently deliver frontier intelligence and bring that as accessibly as possible with every model generation."

— Dianne Penn, Anthropic Product Leader

Performance and Positioning

Opus has historically occupied the middle tier of Anthropic's Claude lineup — more capable and expensive than Sonnet, but cheaper than the company's flagship models. Opus 4.8, priced at $5 per million input tokens and $25 per million output tokens, had already established itself as the default coding agent across tools like Cursor, Windsurf, and GitHub Copilot.

https://youtube.com/watch?v=POIbM1_kxBY

Opus 5 pushes that performance closer to Fable 5, which commands $10 per million input tokens and $50 per million output tokens. For the vast majority of enterprise use cases — code reviews, knowledge retrieval, document analysis — Penn suggested Opus 5 offers the better value proposition.

"Users should pick Opus 5 for value and Fable 5 for 'days-long, very autonomous projects,'" Penn told Reuters.

Safety and Guardrails

In internal testing, Anthropic found Opus 5 was less capable of exploiting cybersecurity vulnerabilities than Fable 5, allowing the company to impose less restrictive safeguards. The model was also less susceptible to being tricked into misuse than Anthropic's other current models, the startup said.

https://x.com/diamai_/status/2080715361742168132

The safety positioning is notable given the recent turbulence around Fable 5. Released in June, the flagship model was temporarily pulled after U.S. authorities raised concerns that its capabilities could be diverted to foreign military intelligence. It returned with usage credits replacing the previous subscription-inclusive access, creating a billing cliff that pushed many developers back to Opus-tier models.

Developer Ecosystem

GitHub announced Opus 5 support in Copilot on the same day, making the model available across Visual Studio Code, JetBrains IDEs, Xcode, and Eclipse. The integration extends Anthropic's reach into the daily workflow of millions of developers who already use Copilot for code generation and review.

The move comes as the competitive landscape for AI coding tools intensifies. OpenAI's GPT-5.6 Sol reached general availability recently, and China-based Moonshot unveiled Kimi K3, an open-weight model that U.S. officials accused of freeloading off Anthropic's research. When asked about Kimi K3, Penn said it "remains to be seen" how open-weight models perform on complicated real-world projects.

Why It Matters for the Indian Tech Community

Anthropic rolled out rupee pricing for Claude in India earlier this month, with the Pro plan starting at Rs 1,999 per month on an annual basis. India now accounts for about 6% of global Claude usage, and the company opened a Bengaluru office this year under former Microsoft India managing director Irina Ghose. A more affordable Opus model could accelerate adoption among Indian startups and enterprise teams already building with Claude's API.

The launch also follows AMD's announcement on Tuesday of a $5 billion strategic equity investment in Anthropic, alongside a deal to deploy up to two gigawatts of AMD Instinct MI450 Series GPUs. The first gigawatt of deployment is set to begin in the first half of 2027, giving Anthropic the compute infrastructure to scale Claude across its growing customer base.
